analyst.summary: Sun Pharma's FY26 print masks a decelerating Q4 (revenue -5.9% QoQ, operating margin -500bps QoQ to 27%, PAT growth flattered by a favorable YoY tax-rate base effect) and management has cut FY27 revenue guidance to high-single-digit growth from FY26's ~12%. Offsetting this, the specialty (Innovative Medicines) franchise is genuinely maturing -- US innovative sales past $1.1bn for the first time in FY26, Leqselvi's Incyte litigation overhang now resolved and monetizing via a July-2025 settlement -- while the April-2026 $11.75bn all-cash Organon acquisition (the largest ever by an Indian pharma company) is a real strategic diversification into biosimilars/global women's health, funded by taking net debt/EBITDA from ~0x to ~2.3x. That debt-funded scale-up arrives while four Sun manufacturing sites (Halol, Dadra, Baska, and an unconfirmed Mohali) carry live or recently-live USFDA compliance actions, Halol's being part of a near-decade recurring pattern. At ~40.8x trailing earnings and ~5.6x book on 14.8% ROE, the market is pricing more growth than current guidance supports; we see no balance-sheet or governance red flag today, but valuation cushion is thin against a genuinely widened regulatory-and-leverage risk stack. Recommendation: Hold, not Sell -- and the desk should treat the Organon deal's leverage step-up as a live monitoring item, not a footnote.
